title: Part V concept map
h1: Part V Concept Map: Ship It
description: An expandable map of Modules 11–12, connecting model routing, caching and cost budgets with deployment, release controls and operational monitoring.
lead: Part V prepares an application for release and operation. Performance choices affect quality, latency and cost; release controls identify what is being deployed; operations observe the running system and provide incident and rollback paths. A passing local check is one input to that work, not a production certification.
story: Use measured routing, caching and budgets to balance latency, quality and cost.
Use reproducible release controls, monitor the live service and respond to incidents.

modules.title: Performance and Cost Optimization
modules.tagline: Measure and tune the work each request performs

topics.title: Routing, caching and batching
topics.definition: Routing selects a model or path, caching reuses eligible results and batching groups work to improve throughput.
topics.example: Route a tested simple task to a smaller deployment and batch independent offline evaluations.
topics.finance: Customer-specific answers require cache isolation and authorization-aware keys before any response is reused.
topics.usecase: Reducing latency or spend while preserving required quality and privacy.
topics.keep: Measure end-to-end effects; caching and batching change freshness, isolation and failure behavior.

topics.title: Cost and latency budgets
topics.definition: A budget sets measurable limits for resource use, response time or error behavior over a defined workload.
topics.example: Estimate monthly input and output token costs from a tested request volume and current provider rates.
topics.finance: A support feature needs a volume estimate, budget owner and a plan for traffic spikes.
topics.usecase: Capacity planning, model selection and cost monitoring.
topics.keep: Estimates depend on workload and rate-card details; include retries, tools, storage and other charges where applicable.

modules.title: Productionizing Generative AI
modules.tagline: Control releases and operate the service after launch

topics.title: Deployment and release controls
topics.definition: Deployment controls package and promote a versioned application and its model, prompts, configuration and dependencies.
topics.example: Record an image digest, model deployment, prompt version, evaluation set and rollback target in a release manifest.
topics.finance: A bank release should be traceable to approved artifacts and a tested rollback path.
topics.usecase: Repeatable promotion through development, test and production environments.
topics.keep: A manifest's shape does not verify artifact provenance, permissions, deployment success or rollback readiness.
connects: capacity and spend depend on release configuration

topics.title: Monitoring, incidents and drift
topics.definition: Operations monitor service health and quality, investigate incidents and detect changes in inputs or outcomes over time.
topics.example: Track latency and error rates alongside citation or evaluation signals, with thresholds and an incident owner.
topics.finance: Investigate a rise in unsupported policy answers and use the approved rollback or disable path when required.
topics.usecase: Keeping a deployed AI feature reliable and accountable.
topics.keep: Operational signals need context, access controls and response procedures; a dashboard alone does not resolve incidents.
connects: monitor route behavior and fallback outcomes
